props.name: decorative
props.description: Purely visual: removes the element from the accessibility tree. Set it whenever the surrounding structure — a heading, whitespace, a card boundary — already communicates the break.

props.name: label
props.description: Label for a meaningful separator, e.g. "or" between two actions. Announced only when the separator is not decorative, because a name on a `role="none"` element is a contradiction.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Axis of the line. Vertical separators need a sized parent.

ai.summary: A hairline between content: a real <hr> that announces itself unless it is purely visual.
whenToUse: Two groups of content need a thematic break between them
A form's sections need dividing without a heading
A vertical rule splits two columns
whenNotToUse: The break is already communicated by a heading or Card boundary — mark it `decorative` or skip it
You are separating items in a list — use spacing or a list style; it is the honest tool
Two routes branch at a choice — use Tabs or a Radio Group to express the choice; "or" between buttons is not a widget
ai.accessibility: Renders a real `<hr>`, announced as a separator by screen readers. `decorative` flips it to `role="none"` for lines that exist only for the eye. A `label` (e.g. "or" between two actions) is announced only when the separator is meaningful — a name on a `role="none"` element is a contradiction. The line is the 1px hairline token, not the 3px chrome stroke: a separator divides content, and a 3px stroke between paragraphs reads as a wall.
knownLimitations: Vertical separators need a sized parent — `align-self: stretch` is the default, not a guarantee
No motion, no chrome, by design — the one component where the hairline is the point
